Subject: Initial MAP ask — acceptance criteria + evaluation tests

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for yesterday's demo. Tom and I talked through the team and procurement asks overnight — we need a concise mutual action plan (MAP) that defines: success criteria for our evaluation, explicit exit gates (what would fail the trial), and a set of acceptance tests we can run against our sampled traffic. Procurement also wants to see an initial SOW and the security questionnaire filled in.

High-level constraints:
- 2-week evaluation starting 2026-06-14
- Sample traffic: 5k inference calls/day, P95 latency target < 450ms for the primary model variant
- PHI redaction pipeline must be demonstrable in the trial environment

Can you share a MAP draft that maps owners for each deliverable (Redwood vs Greenleaf), the acceptance test definitions, and what success looks like on day 14? If you can also surface the SOW draft and point us to the security questionnaire, that would speed procurement.

Thanks,

Greenleaf Health

Subject: Re: Initial MAP ask — acceptance criteria + evaluation tests

Elena — thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a first-pass MAP workbook (MAP-v1.xlsx) and a short SOW stub (Greenleaf-SOW-draft.pdf). Below is a concise acceptance storyboard and owner matrix so procurement and your engineering team can align quickly.

Quick summary (two-page rundown):
1) Primary success signals (must all be true to consider trial a success):
   - Functional: Model accuracy on Greenleaf anchor set >= 88% (measured by your labeled subset)
   - Performance: P95 latency observed < 450ms under 5k calls/day load profile
   - Safety: PHI redaction rate >= 99% on synthetic PHI injection tests, zero production telemetry leakage
   - Operational: < 1% token error rate, no sustained (>15 min) availability < 99.5%

2) Exit gates (immediate stop conditions):
   - Any verified PHI exposure incident during trial (stop + joint incident review)
   - Mean inference errors > 3% for 24h window (systemic regression)
   - Repeated SLA violations: 3 P95 latency breaches in 48 hours

3) Acceptance tests (ownership and pass criteria):
   - Accuracy check (Greenleaf): Greenleaf runs labeled batch (owner: Greenleaf) -> Redwood runs evaluation pipeline and returns metrics and confusion matrix (pass: accuracy >= 88).
   - Load & latency smoke (Redwood): Redwood runs synthetic load per profile against the trial endpoint for 4 hours (pass: P95 < 450ms).
   - PHI redaction injection (joint): Greenleaf provides 500 synthetic documents with varied PHI patterns; Redwood runs redaction and reports false negatives (pass: FN <= 1%).
   - End-to-end integration test (joint): Validate data ingress, model inference, and artifact sanitation on staging (pass: no auth/permission failures; sample traces show no raw PHI in logs).

4) Owners & timeline (two-week eval window starting 2026-06-14):
   - Week 0 (preflight, by 2026-06-11): finalize SOW (Redwood: Camila), finalize MAP workbook and test vectors (Greenleaf: Elena), security questionnaire completed (Redwood sec + Greenleaf sec).
   - Week 1 (2026-06-14 to 06-20): baseline accuracy test & PHI injection, initial load smoke, telemetry setup (owners: R: Karthik + Camila, G: Elena + Tom).
   - Week 2 (06-21 to 06-28): monitor at production-like volume, run acceptance batch, handoff review (owners: joint). Decision meeting scheduled 06-29.

5) Evidence deliverables (what we'll provide): MAP-v1.xlsx (ownership and tasks), trial endpoints and runbook, 24h telemetry dashboard link, acceptance results report (accuracy + latency + safety).

Next steps: Camila will share the SOW and MAP workbook in Drive; Karthik can add the load-profile details and the exact telemetry dashboards. Can you confirm the proposed 2-week window and that your labeled anchor set will be available by 2026-06-11?

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP-v1.xlsx (stub), Greenleaf-SOW-draft.pdf (stub)

Adding a quick technical note on load & observability so acceptance tests are executable and reproducible.

- Load profile (we will provide): 5k calls/day average with a 2x burst window of 2 hours. We'll attach JMeter config and a short python harness in the Drive folder.
- Telemetry: we'll instrument per-request metadata (route, model-version, seq-len, token-count) and provide a P95 latency breakdown by model & route. That will be used as evidence for the performance pass criterion.
- Canary & fallback: during the trial we'll run 5% of production traffic through the trial endpoint first; automatic fallback rule will switch 100% back to baseline if any safety exit gate triggers.

Proposed measurable acceptance artifact (deliverable names):
- accuracy_report_GLH_20260621.csv (Redwood produced after Greenleaf labeled batch)
- latency_trace_P95_20260620.png (dashboard snapshot)
- phi_injection_report_20260619.xlsx (joint)

I'll also flag one pragmatic adjustment: if Greenleaf wants to reduce the P95 latency target to 400ms we should consider a small quantized variant and list it as an alternate path (cost vs latency tradeoff). If you want, Camila and I can sketch the variant options in the MAP workbook.

-karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
